title: Longtime sports analyst Rob Parker not sold that Red Sox will make playoffs
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Rob Parker doubts the Red Sox will maintain their current performance and qualify for the playoffs.
The Red Sox have a 64-52 record, holding the second A.L. wild-card spot with a 96% playoff probability.
FanGraphs estimates the Red Sox have a 12.6% chance of winning the A.L. East and 83.4% for a wild-card berth.

title: Chad Tracy ‘hopeful’ Wilyer Abreu is back in Red Sox lineup Sunday
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Wilyer Abreu was scratched from Saturday's Red Sox lineup due to leg swelling from being hit on Friday.
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy is hopeful Abreu will return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Athletics.
Abreu has 20 home runs and 62 RBIs in 2026, ranking him second in both categories on the team.

title: Red Sox’ latest winning streak ends at 9 games after loss to Athletics
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox' nine-game winning streak ends with 7-3 loss to Athletics, their sixth loss in 38 games.
Jake Bennett allowed four earned runs over 5.1 innings; Boston left 12 runners on base during the game.
Despite the loss, Red Sox maintain the second American League wild-card spot, 1.5 games behind the Yankees.

title: Here’s why Gillette Stadium is swapping out its turf surface again so soon after the World Cup
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Gillette Stadium is replacing its turf again due to a procedural NFL rule requiring specific field testing protocols.
The initial post-World Cup turf, meeting FIFA and NFL standards, wasn't lab-tested and thus non-compliant with NFL requirements.
The new turf will be the pre-World Cup version, as an updated test isn't possible until early 2027.

title: 4 takeaways from the Revolution’s loss vs. Houston Dynamo
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: New England Revolution lost 2-0 to Houston Dynamo at Gillette Stadium, with goals by Guilherme and Agustin Resch.
Jack Harrison made his debut as a Designated Player for New England, entering in the 55th minute as a substitute.
Houston Dynamo's defense held firm as New England struggled to create chances, particularly in wide areas during the match.

title: Here’s the latest injury updates on Roman Anthony, Adley Rutschman
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Roman Anthony is progressing in his recovery from a wrist injury, now hitting off pitching machines with high velocity.
Adley Rutschman recently began a rehab stint with the Worcester Red Sox, catching for five innings and demonstrating defensive skills.
The Red Sox are on a 9-game winning streak and expect lineup boosts with Rutschman and Anthony returning from injuries.

title: New on Netflix and more: Top streaming picks for August 2026
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Clueless', 'Eighth Grade', and 'Something's Gotta Give' are highlighted as top Netflix picks for August.
'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' and 'The Ballad of Wallis Island' among other recommended movies this month.
Staff picks include 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' and 'Ted Lasso' for compelling new season debuts.

title: An 8-foot Bigfoot was spotted in Connecticut last month. It’s far from New England’s first.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A reported Bigfoot sighting in Voluntown, Connecticut, involved an eight-foot creature seen by Kevin Klimas on July 5.
The Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization has verified 126 sightings in New England since 1994, supporting Bigfoot existence claims.
Experts highlight a lack of scientific evidence for Bigfoot, attributing sightings to human belief in extraordinary phenomena.

title: I will miss my friend Margo, who told me to grieve, but not too much
author: Meredith Goldstein
bullets: Margo Howard, daughter of advice columnist Ann Landers, died last month at age 86.
Margo Howard was known for writing Dear Prudence for Slate and Dear Margo for The Boston Globe.
Margo offered practical and sometimes sarcastic advice, encouraging moving past grief for happiness.

title: Red Sox bats, Payton Tolle’s 14 strikeouts stifle Athletics, 13-1
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Payton Tolle struck out 14 batters in the Red Sox's 13-1 victory over the Oakland Athletics.
The Red Sox extended their winning streak to nine games, improving their season record to 64-51.
Boston's offense recorded 15 hits, featuring high-scoring innings to secure the dominant win.
